analyses.failure: test_chk_014_nominal_latency/per=1 — [small.s1] CHK-014: o_full=0 expected at the edge of word 1 got 1 (test_async_gray_fifo.py:430)
analyses.spec_says: REQ-FUNC-008 (spec:137): full 'shall be 1 whenever the write domain has no free entry, judged from the synchronized read pointer ... It may stay 1 late after a read frees an entry (pessimistic).' REQ-FUNC-007 (spec:136): the minimum depth is 2. REQ-VER-001 (spec:181) / DEC-012 (spec:1479): with the model on, a crossing becomes visible at destination edge S..S+2. The CHK-014 contract (contract.json:560-561) is written for DEPTH=8 with the model off: 'Fill to 8 words ... After the 8th write edge, o_full=1 at once.' It says nothing about DEPTH=2 or about the time between the read of xfer and the fill.
analyses.rtl_does: m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:35 sets LPARA_FULL_MSK = 3<<(PTR_W-2). For PTR_W=2 that is 2'b11, which is correct: full means wbin == rbin_s+DEPTH. Line 106: w_full_n = (reg_wgray == w_rgray_s ^ MSK). Line 125: o_full = w_wr_blk | w_full_n. In small.s1 (DEPTH=2, log line 27 '-GPARA_AFIFO_DEPTH=2', model on), xfer has just read one word, so the read pointer is 1. The write domain can still hold the old synchronized value rgray_s=00, because that crossing takes 2..4 write edges with the model. After word 0, wbin=2 (Gray 11) and 11 == 00^11, so the write-domain estimate is 2 = DEPTH and o_full=1 at the word-1 edge. This is the pessimistic 'late fall' that the spec allows. With DEPTH=8 the same staleness only gives an estimate of 2 < 8, which is why every other run passes.
analyses.test_does: test_chk_014_nominal_latency (py:690-704) loops: xfer() (write one word, read it; py:400-419), then idle(nw=randint(0,5)) (py:702), then fill_tr (py:422-452). fill_tr writes DEPTH words at consecutive write edges (py:426) and asserts o_full==0 at every one of those edges (py:428-430). The expectation assumes the read done in xfer has already crossed to the write domain. Nothing waits for that: nw can be 0, and per=1 uses wr=14 ns / rd=6 ns, so word 1 is sampled only 1-3 write edges after the read edge, while the crossing window is S..LMAX = 2..4 edges (py:47-48).

candidates.evidence_for: Fails only in small.s1 (DEPTH=2). It passes in all 13 DEPTH=8 runs, including the other model-on seeds (results.json:55-82). The o_full=1 seen matches the stale-pointer case that the spec explicitly allows (REQ-FUNC-008 'may stay 1 late'). fill_tr has no wait between the previous read and the first write (py:426), although the test itself defines LMAX=S+2 (py:48). The CHK-005/006 scoreboards report no error in small.s1 (results.json CHK-005/006 small.s1 fails=0), so the flag was pessimistic, not wrong.
candidates.evidence_against: The test author may have meant fill_tr to start from a settled FIFO, and the contract stimulus 'at random phases' could be read as allowing any gap. However, it does not allow an expectation that contradicts REQ-FUNC-008.

candidates.evidence_for: The CHK-014 contract (contract.json:560-561) hard-codes DEPTH=8 ('Fill to 8 words', i_full_thr=8) and the model off. The run set nevertheless runs it with DEPTH=2 and the model on (small.s1). The contract does not say how the expectation scales, or how long to wait after the previous read.
candidates.evidence_against: The spec itself is clear that o_full may fall late (spec:137, spec:478). The ambiguity is only in how the contract applies to other parameter values.

candidates.evidence_for: o_full=1 is observed with only one word stored.
candidates.evidence_against: The full compare (wr.sv:106) with the mask (wr.sv:35) is correct for PTR_W=2. o_full=1 follows from a read-pointer value still inside the synchronizer, which REQ-FUNC-008 and spec:478 ('can differ from the true occupancy only by the pointer updates still inside the synchronizer') allow. No scoreboard error was raised.

analyses.options: Fix test: in fill_tr (py:422), before the first write, wait until the last read has crossed, e.g. await tb.idle(nw=LMAX + 2) (or tb.settle). The FIFO is already empty after xfer, so this keeps every check on o_full and only removes the race. Alternatively, compute the expected o_full per edge from the reads whose crossing window S..LMAX has not yet elapsed. Clarify spec/contract: state that CHK-014's fill expectation assumes the write domain has seen all earlier reads, and how 'Fill to 8' scales to PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH. No RTL change is indicated.

analyses.failure: test_chk_021_underflow — [small.s1] CHK-021: write of 0x1 expected accepted (o_full=0) got o_full=1 (py:405 via scn_021 py:542)
analyses.spec_says: REQ-FUNC-008 (spec:137): full is judged from the synchronized read pointer and may stay 1 late after a read (pessimistic). REQ-FUNC-004 (spec:133): a write is accepted only when full=0. The contract CHK-021 stimulus (contract.json:715) is DEPTH=8 and model off: 'write W0..W7, read all 8, write W8, read it.' It gives no settle time between the last read and W8.
analyses.rtl_does: With DEPTH=2, scn_021 writes 2 words and reads both at consecutive read edges, so the read Gray pointer goes 00->01->11. The write domain needs 2..4 write edges per change. If neither change has crossed (w_rgray_s=00), then for the next write wbin=2 (Gray 11): wr.sv:106 gives 11 == 00^11, so w_full_n=1 and o_full=1 (wr.sv:125). The write is not accepted (wr.sv:109) and no word is lost or corrupted. With DEPTH=8, reading 8 words takes 8 read edges, so by the end the write side has already seen most of the reads and the estimate is below 8.
analyses.test_does: scn_021 (py:529-542) writes DEPTH words, waits LMAX+3 read edges, and reads DEPTH words at consecutive read edges (py:537). It waits only for the read records (py:539-541). It then calls xfer (py:542) at once, which writes at the next write edge (py:403) and asserts o_full==0 (py:405). The expectation assumes the write domain has already seen all DEPTH reads.

candidates.evidence_for: Fails only in small.s1 (results.json:314-343) and passes in all DEPTH=8 runs. candidates.evidence_for: The contract stimulus/expected for CHK-021 (contract.json:715-716) is literal for DEPTH=8 ('W0..W7', 'pointer value 9', 'entry 1') and model off. The run set applies it to DEPTH=2 with the model on without defining a settle time.

analyses.failure: test_chk_025_srst_partial_fifo — [small.s1] CHK-025: (4) o_underflow must stay 0 while i_rst_n_sw=0 (py:1128; E[u-1].tr=2096823582 ps < Wr[H].tr=2096986738 ps)
analyses.spec_says: REQ-SRST-003 (spec:162): a read is blocked only 'while the synchronized request is 1, or the read reset FSM is not in RUN'. REQ-SRST-017 (spec:176): 'a blocked write or read shall not raise o_overflow or o_underflow'. REQ-ERR-002 (spec:159): a read requested while empty raises the underflow pulse. REQ-SRST-014 (spec:173) / spec:756: reads before the request reaches the read domain are normal reads. The contract CHK-025 stimulus (contract.json:849-850) is literal for DEPTH=8: 'write D0..D5 ... Drive i_rd_en=1 at every read edge from W0', and expected (4) 'While i_rst_n_sw=0, o_underflow stays 0'. That expectation assumes the FIFO still holds words until the block arrives.
analyses.rtl_does: With DEPTH=2 only D0 and D1 are accepted; D2..D5 are rejected because o_full=1. From W0, i_rd_en=1 at every read edge, so the reads at e1 and e1+1 drain the FIFO. The request (req_wr, set with busy, wr.sv:203-205,216-221) crosses through u_sync_req and becomes w_req_s at read edge S..S+2 = 2..4 (rd.sv:218-227). Before that, w_rd_blk=0 (rd.sv:93), so a read on the now really empty FIFO gives reg_underflow <= i_rd_en & ~w_rd_blk & w_empty_n = 1 (rd.sv:154). That is a normal underflow, not a blocked read. The failing record is ~37 ns after W0 and 163 ns (about 16 write cycles) before H=W0+20. This matches an underflow at read edge ~3 after W0, before the block.
analyses.test_does: py:1066-1074: ft=min(6,TMAX), writes 6 words without checking acceptance, then waits 5+EXTRA read edges. rdrv (py:1078-1086) sets i_rd_en=1 at every read edge. py:1119 L=lead(E,'o_empty',0): this is the number of leading edges with o_empty=0. With DEPTH=2 that is 2, because the FIFO is empty, not because it is blocked. py:1124 u = first underflow at or after L. py:1128 asserts that this underflow comes after H. The test treats every o_empty=1 after L as 'blocked', which only holds when the FIFO has more than S+2 words.

candidates.evidence_for: With DEPTH=2 the FIFO cannot keep words until the request reaches the read domain (up to S+2=4 read edges with reads at every edge), so the scenario precondition is not met. The test writes 6 words (py:1070-1072) but only DEPTH=2 are accepted, and it does not check this. The underflow occurs ~37 ns after W0, before any block is possible, and rd.sv:154 raises it exactly as REQ-ERR-002 requires for an unblocked read of an empty FIFO. The CHK-002 checker (contract.json:268) and the scoreboards report no error in small.s1. Passes in all DEPTH=8 runs.
candidates.evidence_against: If the underflow happened after the request had reached the read domain it would be an RTL bug. The timing (~37 ns after W0 vs a minimum crossing of 2 read edges = 28 ns after W1=W0+1 write edge) is close. Without a waveform the exact read edge cannot be confirmed from the logs alone.

candidates.evidence_for: The contract for CHK-025 (contract.json:849-850) uses DEPTH=8 constants (D0..D5, i_full_thr=6) and the model off. Expected (4) is valid only if the FIFO is still non-empty when the block arrives. The contract does not define the scenario for DEPTH < S+3.
candidates.evidence_against: The spec rules for what is blocked (spec:162,176) are precise. The open question is only the test's applicability to small depths.

candidates.evidence_for: o_underflow pulsed while i_rst_n_sw=0.
candidates.evidence_against: REQ-SRST-017 forbids pulses only for blocked reads. The block is defined by the synchronized request (REQ-SRST-003), which lags by S..S+2 read edges. The pulse timing points to an unblocked read of an empty FIFO. CHK-002 (which allows pulses only for i_rd_en & o_empty) shows 0 failures in small.s1.

analyses.options: Fix test, option 1 (stimulus): write min(6, DEPTH) words and check that each was accepted. Start the always-on reads only so that the FIFO is still non-empty at read edge S+2 after W1, e.g. by enabling reads from read edge S+3 after W1 when DEPTH < S+3. Then expectation (4) keeps its meaning. Fix test, option 2 (expectation derived from spec): compute u from the first underflow after the block has started, i.e. after the first read edge where o_empty=1 while the FIFO still held pre-reset words or after read edge LMAX. Treat underflow pulses at edges before the request can have crossed as normal REQ-ERR-002 pulses. Clarify contract: state the minimum DEPTH for CHK-025, or express the D0..D5 / thresholds in terms of DEPTH. Optionally confirm with a waveform that the pulse's read edge is earlier than the w_req_s rise (rd.sv:226). If it is not, the cause moves to A.

analyses.failure: CHK-003 assertion — o_empty_thr consistency (590 fails; 0 in model_off.s1 and syn.s1; first fail 231868000 ps in base.s1)
analyses.spec_says: REQ-FUNC-010 (spec:139): o_empty_thr = 1 when the read-domain occupancy estimate <= i_empty_thr; the estimate is pessimistic. Section 9 (spec:477): 'An invalid Gray value cannot occur in the model with one-bit changes'. spec:478: the estimate 'can differ from the true occupancy only by the pointer updates still inside the synchronizer'. INV-001 (spec:240): 0..DEPTH. In contrast, REQ-VER-001 (spec:181) and DEC-012 (spec:1479) say the model 'randomizes the latency of each bit independently' (extra 0..2 destination cycles, with a pending change replaced by a new one). Section 10.6.4 (spec:684) justifies this by assuming 'A Gray pointer changes one bit per update, so a late bit makes the destination domain see the previous pointer value'. DEC-023 (spec:1491): 'the destination sees only valid Gray values at any frequency'. Contract CHK-003 (contract.json:287): (a) o_empty -> o_empty_thr; (b) i_empty_thr >= DEPTH -> o_empty_thr=1; (c) thr==0 -> o_empty_thr==o_empty.
analyses.rtl_does: rd.sv:104-112: w_wbin_s = Gray->binary(w_wgray_s), w_occ = w_wbin_s - reg_rbin. rd.sv:117-118: o_empty = w_rd_blk | (reg_rgray==w_wgray_s), o_empty_thr = w_rd_blk ? 1 : (w_occ <= i_empty_thr). For any synchronized value, (a) and (c) always hold: equal Gray means occ=0. So only (b) can fail, which requires w_occ > DEPTH. A coherent, monotonically lagging wbin_s always gives 0 <= occ <= DEPTH, so a failure needs a non-sequential wbin_s. The model in m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:145-182 delays each bit independently by 0..2 extra cycles (lines 158-177). When the write pointer changes more than one bit within that window (back-to-back writes), a later-changed bit can overtake an earlier one. Example: 0010->0110->0111 seen as 0011 = binary 2, i.e. backwards, so occ = 2 - rbin can wrap to 15. With the model off, o_q = plain chain (line 182) and there are no fails.
analyses.test_does: The SVA in nnc_chk_rd.sv:73-77 checks (a),(b),(c) at every i_clk_rd edge, which is a direct coding of contract.json:287. The failures fall in random-traffic tests where the write clock is as fast as or faster than the read clock, e.g. base.s1 231-343 us = CHK-016 pair=2 (10/23 ns, py:751, sim.log:68-74). i_empty_thr is random per pair (py:761). No software reset is in progress (run_traffic sw=False, py:770).

candidates.evidence_for: The spec mandates per-bit independent random delays (REQ-VER-001 spec:181, DEC-012 spec:1479, spec:653), while also stating that only valid Gray values / previous pointer values are seen (spec:477, spec:684, DEC-023 spec:1491) and that the estimate is pessimistic (spec:139,478). These conflict when the source pointer changes faster than the 2-cycle extra-delay window, which the spec explicitly allows ('no restriction on the frequency or the frequency ratio', REQ-CLK-001 spec:149). The fail pattern fits: 0 fails in model_off.s1 and syn.s1 with identical stimulus, CHK-003 fails during write-faster phases, and CHK-013 (write side) during read-faster phases. REQ-FUNC-014 (spec:143) forbids modelling outside the per-bit wrapper, so the RTL cannot make the model vector-coherent without a spec decision.
candidates.evidence_against: One could argue the spec's 'independent per bit' wording is deliberate and the requirements already settle the issue. But then the spec's own invariants (spec:477-478, INV-001, TEST-008 'flags never optimistic' spec:1246) do not hold, so the spec is internally inconsistent either way.

candidates.evidence_for: The model is RTL code (rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:98-183) and it produces synchronized pointer values the source never held in sequence. In silicon only the bit changing in the setup window is uncertain, so the destination sees the current or the previous Gray value. A model that lets a later bit change overtake an earlier pending one is less faithful than the spec's stated intent (spec:684-685).
candidates.evidence_against: The model follows the letter of REQ-VER-001/DEC-012 (independent random latency per bit, replacement of pending changes, edges S..S+2: lines 146-177 match spec:181). The FIFO logic itself (rd.sv:112,117-118) is an exact implementation of REQ-FUNC-010 and is correct for every coherent input. With the model off there are 0 fails.

candidates.evidence_for: (b) assumes the estimate never exceeds DEPTH.
candidates.evidence_against: That assumption is stated by the spec (INV-001 spec:240, spec:478, REQ-FUNC-010 pessimism). The SVA matches contract.json:287 exactly. The checker is not wrong relative to the spec. (The 'and while i_rst_n_rd=0' wording is harmless: in reset o_empty=o_empty_thr=1.)

analyses.options: Clarify spec (needed first): decide whether the metastability model must keep a multi-bit Gray crossing coherent, i.e. the destination only sees values the source pointer actually held, in order. Then reconcile REQ-VER-001/DEC-012/10.6.4 with spec:477-478, INV-001, DEC-023 and TEST-008. If coherence is required, fix the RTL model in m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv. For example, bound the extra delay so that a pending bit change is never applied after a later change of another bit. Because each wrapper is one bit and REQ-FUNC-014 forbids modelling in m_vlsit_afifo_sync, this may also need a spec change allowing a vector-level model or a per-crossing seed/ordering rule. If the spec instead keeps fully independent per-bit delays, the FIFO cannot meet the pessimism and INV-001 requirements under that model, and the requirement owners must restate what the model is meant to verify. Do not relax CHK-003. To confirm, dump w_wgray_s and reg_rbin at a failing edge (e.g. 231868 ns in base.s1) and check that w_occ > DEPTH.

analyses.failure: CHK-005 assertion — scoreboard show-ahead/order/software-reset discard (16 fails, all in cell4.s1; first 1183353000 ps)
analyses.spec_says: REQ-SRST-014 (spec:173): 'A read accepted before the request reaches the read domain returns a valid pre-reset word.' spec:756 repeats this. REQ-SRST-002 (spec:161): the request crosses through m_vlsit_afifo_sync 'the same stage count as the pointers'. REQ-FUNC-013 (spec:142): S=4 for option 4. REQ-VER-001 (spec:181): the output changes at edge S, S+1 or S+2. So with PARA_AFIFO_CELL_TYPE=4, pre-reset reads are legal up to read edge S+2=6 after the busy rise. The contract CHK-005 (contract.json:342) hard-codes the discard point as 'At read edge S+3=5', which is correct only for S=2.
analyses.rtl_does: wr.sv:202-221: busy and req_wr rise at the same write edge. rd.sv:218-227 synchronizes req with S=4 stages plus 0..2 model cycles (cell_sync.sv:99-100,146-177), so w_req_s rises at read edge 4..6. rd.sv:93: reads are blocked only from then on, so a read sampled at edge 6 can still be accepted and shows the head pre-reset word. This is the REQ-SRST-014 behaviour.
analyses.test_does: The SVA reference model nnc_chk_sb.sv:71-77 deletes P when sw_cnt >= 5, a fixed literal that ignores PARA_AFIFO_CELL_TYPE. At the next read edge (6), a legal pre-reset read with o_empty=0 meets s_have=0 (P cleared, Q empty because writes are blocked), so a_CHK_005 (line 97) fails. The cocotb scoreboard implements the same rule with S from the cell type: py:43 S=4 for CT=4, py:194 and py:212 clear at pc >= S+3 = 7. It reported no error: every cell4.s1 test passed (cell4 log line 390 'PASS=34 FAIL=0').

candidates.evidence_for: The checker uses the literal 5 (nnc_chk_sb.sv:73) instead of S+3 with S from PARA_AFIFO_CELL_TYPE. Fails only in cell4.s1 (S=4); 0 fails in base (S=2) and cell3 (S=3, where edge S+2=5 is still covered) (results.json:1016-1079). Every failure is in a test with software resets: CHK-017 run_traffic sw=True at 1183-1203 us, CHK-029 1291-1487 us, CHK-030 1492 us, CHK-031 1495 us, regression_random 1515/1571 us (cell4 log lines 96-346, 261-435). The cocotb scoreboard with S+3=7 passes the same traffic. CHK-006 fails at exactly the same timestamps, from the same cleared-P state.
candidates.evidence_against: The checker literally implements the contract text 'S+3=5' (contract.json:342), so relative to the contract it is 'right'. The contract is what is wrong for S=4.

candidates.evidence_for: contract.json:342 fixes 'S+3=5'. CHK-029 expected (contract.json:935) says 'no pre-reset word is read after read edge 4 following the busy rise' (S+2 for S=2 only). Both are written for cell option 2, yet the run set includes cell4.
candidates.evidence_against: The spec itself is consistent: S depends on the cell option (spec:142), the request uses the same stage count (spec:161), and pre-reset reads are legal until the request arrives (spec:173). Only the derived contract text is S=2-specific.

candidates.evidence_for: Pre-reset words are still shown and read at read edge 6 after the busy rise.
candidates.evidence_against: For S=4 with the model, the request arrives at edge 4..6 (spec:181), and REQ-SRST-014 makes those reads legal. There are 0 fails in cell3 and base. The cocotb scoreboard, which is S-aware, finds no data error in cell4.s1.

No RTL change is indicated.

analyses.failure: CHK-006 assertion — flags never optimistic / occupancy bound (16 fails, all in cell4.s1, same timestamps as CHK-005; first 1183353000 ps)
analyses.spec_says: REQ-FUNC-009 (spec:138): empty 'shall never be 0 while the FIFO is physically empty'. REQ-SRST-014 (spec:173): before the request reaches the read domain the FIFO still holds valid pre-reset words that may be read. For S=4 that lasts up to read edge S+2=6 (REQ-FUNC-013 spec:142, REQ-VER-001 spec:181). Contract CHK-006 (contract.json:365) uses P from CHK-005: '(b) if N == 0 and P is empty, then o_empty=1'. P is cleared 'At read edge S+3=5' (contract.json:342).
analyses.rtl_does: As for CHK-005. At read edge 6 after the busy rise, with S=4 and the model's extra delay, w_req_s can still be 0 (rd.sv:93,218-227). Pre-reset words remain in the FIFO, so o_empty=0 (rd.sv:117) is physically correct.
analyses.test_does: nnc_chk_sb.sv:106 a_CHK_006_r requires o_empty=1 when s_n==0 and s_pempty. P was deleted at sw_cnt >= 5 (line 73-76), one read edge too early for S=4, and Q is empty because writes are blocked. The assertion therefore fires at the read edge where the DUT legitimately still shows a pre-reset word, at the same time as a_CHK_005 (cell4 log lines 261-262, 265-266, ... 434-435).

All 16 CHK-006 failures coincide exactly with the 16 CHK-005 failures and occur only in cell4.s1 during software-reset tests. The S-aware Python scoreboard (py:194,212, CHK-006 checks at py:198-201,217-218) reports nothing.

analyses.options: Fix checker: the same one-line change as CHK-005 (P discard at S+3 with S derived from PARA_AFIFO_CELL_TYPE in nnc_chk_sb.sv:73). CHK-006 then needs no change of its own. Clarify contract: parameterise 'S+3=5' and 'PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH (8)' in contract.json:342/365. No RTL change is indicated.

analyses.failure: CHK-013 assertion — o_full_thr consistency (748 fails; 0 in model_off.s1 and syn.s1; first fail 8648000 ps in base.s1)
analyses.spec_says: REQ-FUNC-010 (spec:139): o_full_thr = 1 when the write-domain occupancy estimate >= i_full_thr; the estimate 'is pessimistic for the full side'. spec:478: it 'can differ from the true occupancy only by the pointer updates still inside the synchronizer'. spec:477: 'An invalid Gray value cannot occur in the model with one-bit changes'. DEC-023 (spec:1491): 'destination sees only valid Gray values at any frequency'. But REQ-VER-001 (spec:181), DEC-012 (spec:1479) and 10.6.4 (spec:653) make each bit's model latency random and independent. Contract CHK-013 (contract.json:524): (a) thr==0 -> 1; (b) thr > DEPTH -> 0; (c) thr==DEPTH -> o_full_thr == (o_full & sw & !busy); (d) o_full & sw & !busy -> o_full_thr == (thr <= DEPTH).
analyses.rtl_does: wr.sv:111-120: w_rbin_s = Gray->binary(w_rgray_s), w_occ = reg_wbin - w_rbin_s. wr.sv:126: o_full_thr = w_wr_blk ? (thr==0) : (w_occ >= thr). wr.sv:106,125: o_full = blk | (wgray == rgray_s ^ MSK), i.e. occ == DEPTH. For any synchronized value, (a) and (d) always hold. (b) and (c) fail only if w_occ > DEPTH. A coherent, monotonically lagging rbin_s always gives occ <= DEPTH, because writes stop at occ == DEPTH. So the failures need a non-sequential w_rgray_s. The per-bit model (m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:158-177, independent 0..2 extra cycles per bit) produces one when the read pointer changes several bits within the window. With the model off (line 182 plain chain) there are 0 fails.
analyses.test_does: The SVA nnc_chk_wr.sv:123-129 is a direct coding of contract.json:524. The failures occur where the read pointer moves quickly relative to i_clk_wr. In base.s1: 8.6-11.6 us is CHK-014 per=1 (wr 14 / rd 6 ns, py:691), 140-212 us is CHK-016 pair=1 (10/10.3), 675-798 us is pair=4 (23/10) (sim.log:42-88,297-363). i_full_thr is DEPTH or random (py:696,761). There are no CHK-013 fails in the write-faster pair=2, where CHK-003 fails instead.

candidates.evidence_for: Same conflict as CHK-003, mirrored to the write side. Per-bit independent latency (spec:181,1479) versus valid-Gray-only / pessimistic estimate (spec:477-478,1491, TEST-008 spec:1246 'flags never optimistic') when the source pointer changes faster than the extra-delay window. REQ-CLK-001 (spec:149) allows any clock ratio. 0 fails in model_off.s1 and syn.s1 with the same stimulus. The fails track read-faster phases, while CHK-003 tracks write-faster phases. Every cell option and depth fails with the model on (results.json:1516-1576).
candidates.evidence_against: The spec could be read as accepting incoherent values as realistic metastability. In that case the spec's own invariants (INV-001 spec:240, spec:477-478) are what must change, so the spec is still inconsistent.

candidates.evidence_for: The synchronizer model (rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:98-183) lets a later bit change of the read Gray pointer reach the write domain before an earlier pending one. The destination then sees pointer values never held in sequence, which a real 2-FF synchronizer with a bounded path delay (DEC-023) does not do.
candidates.evidence_against: The model follows REQ-VER-001/DEC-012 literally (independent per-bit latency S..S+2, replacement of pending changes). The threshold logic wr.sv:120,126 implements REQ-FUNC-010 exactly and is correct for any coherent input. The write-block branch is checked separately by CHK-009, which has 0 fails.

candidates.evidence_for: (b) and (c) assume the estimate never exceeds DEPTH.
candidates.evidence_against: That assumption comes from the spec (INV-001, spec:478, REQ-FUNC-010 'pessimistic'). The SVA matches the contract. Failures vanish when the model is off, so the checker logic is not the source.

analyses.options: Clarify spec: decide whether the model must keep multi-bit Gray crossings coherent (destination sees only values the source held, in order) and reconcile REQ-VER-001/DEC-012/10.6.4 with spec:477-478, INV-001, DEC-023 and TEST-008. Fix RTL after that decision: change the simulation branch of m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv (lines 146-182) so that a later bit change cannot be applied before an earlier pending one of the same pointer. This may need the spec to allow ordering information or a vector-level model, given REQ-FUNC-014. Do not relax CHK-013. To confirm, at a failing edge (e.g. 8648 ns in base.s1) dump w_rgray_s and reg_wbin and check that w_occ > DEPTH and that w_rgray_s is not a value the read pointer held in sequence.
